issues.description: Method Milkable.messageOnMilk(): the problem statement (UML and textual instructions) specifies messageOnMilk() should return a String containing the text "[Animal Type] [name] is milked". The template Main calls System.out.println(m.messageOnMilk()), which also implies a String return. However, the solution repository defines the interface method as boolean messageOnMilk() (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Milkable.java) and the implementing classes Seal and Goat implement it by printing the milking message to stdout and returning true (Seal.messageOnMilk() and Goat.messageOnMilk()). This mismatched return type and behavior (boolean + side-effect printing vs. required String return) will confuse students, cause inconsistent usage in examples/tests, and may break compilation or test expectations depending on which API is assumed.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the API consistent with the problem statement: change the Milkable interface signature to 'String messageOnMilk();'. Update Seal and Goat to return the milking message string (e.g., "Seal Clarabelle is milked" / "Goat Buttinsky is milked") instead of printing and returning boolean. Update any callers (e.g., Main and tests) to print the returned String (System.out.println(m.messageOnMilk())) if they should display it. This preserves the educational intent and aligns UML/text, template usage, and implementation.

issues.description: The method Milkable.messageOnMilk represents the milking action. In the problem statement (UML and narrative) Milkable.messageOnMilk() is specified to return a String (the text even specifies it should return "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"), and the template Main.java calls System.out.println(m.messageOnMilk()) expecting a printable String. In the solution repository, Milkable is declared as boolean messageOnMilk(), and Seal and Goat implement it by printing the milking message and returning true. This is a direct API mismatch: the problem and template expect a String-returning method, while the solution provides a boolean-returning method that performs the printing. Students cannot reliably map the required behavior to the provided solution API (returning a String vs returning a boolean and printing internally), which will cause confusion and potential test/design failures.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the Milkable.messageOnMilk API across artifacts. Preferred fix: change the solution to declare 'String messageOnMilk();' in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Milkable.java and update implementations (Seal, Goat) to return the string "[Animal Type] [name] is milked" (do not print inside the method). This aligns with the UML and the template's System.out.println(m.messageOnMilk()) usage. Alternatively (less recommended), update the problem statement and template to document and expect a boolean-returning messageOnMilk() that performs printing internally; however, this reduces clarity and deviates from the UML/text expectation.
